intro.title: Trapping Rain Water
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a function to calculate how much rainwater can be trapped between bars of different heights, a classic problem in algorithm design. You will learn the core concept of using two pointers to efficiently scan the array from both ends, comparing heights to determine water capacity at each position. The main technologies involved are JavaScript arrays, loops, conditional logic, and the two-pointer technique. By the end, you will understand how to solve this problem step-by-step and implement a working solution in JavaScript.
intro.usecase: The Trapping Rain Water algorithm is essential in real-world applications like urban planning software, where it helps model water accumulation in terrain or city landscapes to design effective drainage systems. In data visualization dashboards, this pattern can be used to represent resource allocation or capacity limits, such as showing storage usage peaks in cloud infrastructure monitoring tools. Developers implement similar logic in UI components like progress bars or gauges that need to calculate filled areas between boundaries, ensuring accurate visual representations of constrained metrics.
